The words

Where the Lord reveals His presence,
Glory lights the sacred place,
And the soul in adoration
Falls before the throne of grace.

Seraphim, and saints in wonder,
Lift their songs where Christ is set,
And employ, in sacred homage,
Harp, and palm, and coronet.

Light of lights, no light approacheth, —
Sun, nor moon, nor stars of night,
Flood the noon-tide and the darkness
With such radiance of delight.

Beauty of the King Immortal!
Ere we rise to where Thou art,
Let the glory of Thy presence
Chase the darkness from our heart.

How to sing it from the solfa

  • Find doh first. Play or hum F and sing d r m f s up from it, so the whole choir has the key in their ears before you start.
  • Pitch the first note. The tune starts on d (F), on the word “Where”, as a pickup before the first full bar.
  • Count the time. 6/4 means six crotchet beats (two dotted minims) in each bar. In the grid every cell is half a crotchet: a dash (–) holds the note before it, and _ is a rest.
  • Know the notes. The tune uses d r m f s l and the chromatic fe. A comma after a note (s,) is the octave below; an apostrophe (d') is the octave above.

About the hymn

John Brownlie translated these words from the Greek service books for Hymns from the Morningland (Paisley, 1911).

The book printed the words without tunes. They are in Eights and Sevens (8.7.8.7), and this page sets them to OMNI DIE; any other Eights and Sevens tune fits them as well.

  • Words: Traditional Greek
  • Translated (1911): John Brownlie (1857–1925)
  • Melody (1631): Gesangbuch, Corner

Tune OMNI DIE (Gesangbuch, Corner); words by Traditional Greek; translated by John Brownlie (1857–1925).

Sung to the same tune: "Come Who Will," the Voice from Heaven, Christ, for Thee a Wreath Adorning, Cross, Reproach, and Tribulation, Father, Breathe an Evening Blessing, Go in Peace! — Serene Dismission, Jesus, Thou Art Mine Forever, O Thou Sun of Glorious Splendor, Part in Peace! Is Day Before Us, Pastor, Thou Art from Us Taken, Praise to Thee, Thou Great Creator, We Have Heard the Wondrous Story.

Questions about Where the Lord Reveals His Presence

What is the doh of Where the Lord Reveals His Presence?

In this version, in F major, doh is F. If your choir sings it in another key, doh moves to the new key note and every solfa syllable stays the same — that is what movable doh means.

What note does Where the Lord Reveals His Presence start on?

It starts on d (F in F major), a pickup on the word “Where” before the first full bar. Find doh first, then sing up or down to d.

Is Where the Lord Reveals His Presence in the public domain?

Yes. John Brownlie died in 1925; the words were in print by 1911 and the music in 1631. Everyone named died before 1955 and both were published before 1929, so the hymn is out of copyright in the UK, the EU, the United States and Nigeria. Modern arrangements and translations can still be under copyright.
